question: D37 candidate B -- does the harness inject a per-track-scaled cotangent at block 47?
reading: the injected cotangent matches the reference to 6e-05 on the single track and 3e-06 on the pair track at block 47, and to within 1.2e-04 at blocks 0 and 23. Nowhere near the 1.18 and 0.89 the per-track factors would require. The harness does not rescale either track.
consequence: candidate A by elimination: the per-track factors are generated INSIDE our block-47 backward, given a correct cotangent AND correct inputs (the forward at that boundary agrees to under 1 % masked on both tracks). So the campaign's worst trunk result is a REAL PORT DEFECT, not an instrument artefact, and D27/D34/D35/D36/D37 all survive. The 1.18 hunt goes back to the top of the queue.
and_it_reverses_my_own_pass-128_call: I dropped the s_fp32_residual arm at pass 128 because I had registered it predicting a SHRUNK gradient and the measured factor was 1.18, inflated. That was the BLOCK-POOLED median, which is dominated by the 41 pair-track tensors. s_fp32_residual touches the SINGLE track only -- and on the single track the measurement is 0.887 (single_transition, n=5) and 0.796 (attn_pair_bias, which also writes s), i.e. DEFLATED by 11-20 %, which is exactly what "per-block updates quantised away by a bf16 residual far larger than them" predicts. I refuted the hypothesis on a number that does not apply to it. The arm is REINSTATED, scoped to the single track.
what_is_now_boxed: block 47 receives a correct cotangent and correct inputs and produces gradients scaled by a constant PER TRACK: pair x1.183 over 41 tensors, single x0.887 over 5. Blocks 0 and 23, same code and config, produce 1.00 on both. The only things that differ are the weights and the activation magnitudes -- s_norm is 367x block 0's at block 47 while z_norm is flat (0.98x). A per-track constant from correct inputs points at whatever is PER-TRACK in the backward: the two residual streams and their dtypes.
